patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null()` to record `SRTP_AES_ICM_128_KEY_LEN_WSALT` instead of `16`, so the same direct-key path allocates a 30-byte master-key buffer. On the fixed original the instrumented `extract_key_alloc` event still executes with `key_size = 30`, satisfying the root obligation even though the later `stream_key_copy` sink is no longer reached.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the null-cipher policy leaves `srtp_crypto_policy_set_null_cipher_hmac_null()`, its `p->cipher_key_len` field must record the full application-supplied key-plus-salt length for `SRTP_NULL_CIPHER`, not the base 16-byte AES key length.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable helper writes `p->cipher_key_len = 16`, so the fuzzer extracts only a 16-byte direct master key even though `srtp_stream_init_keys()` later requires 30 bytes for the same null-cipher session. The fixed original records `SRTP_AES_ICM_128_KEY_LEN_WSALT`, making the required assertion genuine on the original witness.

nodes.state: The direct-key extraction allocates `ret` with `key_size` equal to the null-cipher policy length, materializing the 16-byte heap buffer later named by AddressSanitizer.
The direct-key branch aliases the same extracted heap buffer into `single_master_key.key` before calling `srtp_stream_init_keys()`.

At the failing `memcpy(tmp_key, key, input_keylen)`, the source pointer `key` is the propagated direct-key buffer and the sink reads more bytes (`input_keylen = 30`) than the null-cipher object was configured with (`rtp_keylen = 16`).

edges.relation: The null-cipher helper's recorded `cipher_key_len` is the `key_size` later passed into `extract_key()`, so the incorrect 16-byte policy length directly controls the master-key allocation size.
The heap buffer returned by `extract_key()` is the same pointer later aliased into `single_master_key.key` for direct stream-key initialization.
The same 16-byte size used to allocate the direct master key is preserved as the null-cipher object's configured `rtp_keylen` when `srtp_stream_init_keys()` reaches the `memcpy` sink.
The aliased `single_master_key.key` pointer becomes the local `key` source argument consumed by the crashing `memcpy()`.
